title: Internet Access: Who's Connected, Who's Not
description: How internet access and digital isolation are distributed across the world, scaled to a global village of 1,000 people.

sections.heading: Digital Isolation Per 1,000 People — Those Without Internet Access
sections.caption: Scaled to a global village of 1,000 people, 247 are completely offline. Africa carries the heaviest burden relative to its size — 109 of the village's ~170 Africans lack internet access, meaning the offline outnumber the online on that continent.
sections.x_label: Number of People Offline (per 1,000 Global Citizens)

sections.heading: Planetary Snapshot: Scaled to 1,000 People
sections.caption: If the entire world's population were scaled down to a village of exactly 1,000 citizens, this table shows the regional split between those with digital access and those living in complete isolation.

sections.heading: Hotspots of Digital Isolation — Countries with the Most Offline People

items.label: India
items.note: Despite a thriving tech sector, a 30% offline rate leaves hundreds of millions disconnected.

items.label: Nigeria
items.note: Even as one of Africa's largest economies, more than half of its citizens do not use the internet.

items.label: Pakistan
items.note: Over half of its population faces barriers related to infrastructure and mobile network quality.

items.label: Ethiopia
items.note: Over 75% of the population is cut off — one of the lowest connectivity rates globally.

items.label: China
items.note: High overall penetration, but its large rural population means millions still wait for access.

items.label: Bangladesh
items.note: Infrastructure gaps and affordability barriers keep nearly half the population disconnected.

items.label: The Sheer Scale
items.note: Nearly 1 out of every 4 people on Earth has never logged onto the web or checked an email.

items.label: The Economic Divide
items.note: High-income nations reach ~94% internet coverage. In low-income economies, only 23% have access — cutting them off from modern economic tools.

items.label: Africa's Digital Gap
items.note: Africa is the only continent where the offline (109 per 1,000) outnumber the online (61 per 1,000).

items.label: The Rural Factor
items.note: In Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, and Burundi, 70–88% of the population lacks access — driven by infrastructure gaps, structural poverty, and lack of grid electricity.
